param-p01.speaker: Śiṣya (student) asks; Guru (Abhinava) answers by Śiva-śāsana view
param-p01.question: What is the supreme principle, and how does the universe relate to it?
premises: Resort (v. 2): paraṃ parasthaṃ gahanād anādim ekaṃ niviṣṭaṃ bahudhā guhāsu | sarvālayaṃ sarvacarācarasthaṃ tvām eva śambhuṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye
Question (v. 3): garbhādhivāsapūrvakamaraṇāntakaduḥkhacakravibhrāntaḥ … ādhāram bhagavantaṃ śiṣyaḥ papraccha paramārtham
Guru's answer (v. 4): ādhārakārikābhiḥ taṃ gurur abhibhāṣati sma tatsāram | kathayaty abhinavaguptaḥ śivaśāsanadṛṣṭiyogena
Fourfold universe (v. 5): nijaśaktivaibhavabharād aṅdacatuṣṭayam idaṃ vibhāgena | śaktir māyā prakṛtiḥ pṛthvī ceti prabhāvitaṃ prabhuṇā
World-continuum (v. 6): tatrāntar viśvam idaṃ vicitratanukaraṇabhuvanasaṃtānam
Experiencer (v. 7): bhoktā ca tatra dehī … śiva eva … gṛhītapaśubhāvaḥ; nānāvidhavarṇānāṃ rūpaṃ dhatte yathāmalaḥ sphaṭikaḥ
Reflection (v. 8): gacchati jala iva himakarabimbaṃ sthite sthitiṃ yāti; rāhur adṛśyo 'pi yathā śaśibimbasthaḥ prakāśate tadvat

Mirror (v. 9): sarvagato 'py ayam ātmā viṣayāśrayaṇena dhīmukure ādarśe malarahite yadvad vadanaṃ vibhāti tadvad ayam; śivaśaktipātavimale dhītattve bhāti bhārūpaḥ; paripūrṇaṃ svātmani viśrāntito mahānandam
param-p01.inference: Śambhu is supreme; the universe is Śiva's fourfold self-manifestation (śakti/māyā/prakṛti/pṛthvī); the experiencer is Śiva veiled (gṛhītapaśubhāvaḥ); the self is like a reflection and like a face in a mirror. Śaktipāta makes the mind stainless; resting in itself, the self is bliss.
param-p01.conclusion: Paramārthasāra opens with Śambhu as supreme, the universe as his fourfold self-manifestation, and the experiencer as Śiva veiled. The mirror and reflection analogies establish that the self is not bound by the body. Śaktipāta is the key to liberation.
param-p01.theorem: The universe = śakti/māyā/prakṛti/pṛthvī, all Śiva's self-manifestation; the experiencer = Śiva veiled (gṛhītapaśubhāvaḥ).
unresolved_terms: aṅdacatuṣṭayam — Abhinava's own schema; not verified against Ādiśeṣa
dṛṣṭi polyvalency (darśana + yogic perception)
param-p01.next_pressure: L2: resort → question → answer → fourfold universe → world-continuum → experiencer (Śiva veiled) → mirror/reflection analogies → śaktipāta → bliss.

param-p02.speaker: Guru (Abhinava)
param-p02.question: What is the supreme tattva, and how do the 36 tattvas relate to it?
premises: Supreme tattva (v. 11): sarvavikalpavihīnaṃ śuddhaṃ śāntaṃ layodayavihīnam | yat paratattvaṃ tasmin vibhāti ṣaṭtriṃśadātma jagat
Mirror analogy (v. 12): darpaṇabimbe yadvan nagaragrāmādicitram avibhāgi | bhāti vibhāgenaiva ca parasparaṃ darpaṇād api ca
Source of reflection (v. 13): vimalatamaparamabhairavabodhāt tadvad vibhāgaśūnyam api | anyonyaṃ ca tato 'pi ca vibhaktam ābhāti jagad etat
Tattva-state (v. 14): śivaśaktisadāśivatām īśvaravidyāmayīṃ ca tattvadaśām
Five Śaktis (v. 15): śaktīnāṃ pañcānāṃ vibhaktabhāvena bhāsayati paramaṃ yat svātantryaṃ durghaṭasaṃpādanaṃ maheśasya
param-p02.inference: The supreme tattva is pure, peaceful, thought-free — and yet the entire 36-fold world shines within it, undivided, like a city reflected in a mirror. The world is not separate from Śiva; it is his self-manifestation (svābhāsa). The five Śaktis (Śiva, Śakti, Sadāśiva, Īśvara, Vidyā) are the tattva-state. Svātantrya makes the division possible without compromising unity.
param-p02.conclusion: Supreme tattva = pure, peaceful, thought-free; 36 tattvas shine in it like mirror-image; Śiva-Śakti-Sadāśiva-Īśvara-Vidyā state; five Śaktis' divided nature produces the world.
param-p02.theorem: paratattva = pure/peaceful/thought-free; jagat = svābhāsa in paratattva, like city in mirror.
unresolved_terms: exact enumeration of 36 tattvas — text names only top five
vimalatamaparamabhairavabodha — Abhinava's yogic perception or tradition's
param-p02.next_pressure: L2: pure tattva → mirror analogy → source of reflection → tattva-state → five Śaktis. Key: v. 13's 'though divisionless, divided.'

param-p03.speaker: Guru (Abhinava)
param-p03.question: How does the supreme consciousness become the embodied experiencer? What is the cosmological descent?
premises: Senses (vv. 20–21): śrotraṃ tvagakṣirasanā ghrāṇaṃ buddhīndriyāṇi śabdādau | vākpāṇipādapāyūpasthaṃ karmendriyāṇi — ten senses, five cognitive + five conative
Tanmātras (v. 22): eṣāṃ grāhyo viṣayaḥ sūkṣmaḥ pravibhāgavarjito yaḥ syāt | tanmātrapañcakaṃ tat śabdaḥ sparśo mahoraso gandhaḥ — five tanmātras: sound, touch, form, taste, smell
Gross elements (v. 23): etatsaṃsargavaśāt sthūlo viṣayas tu bhūtapañcakatām | abhyeti nabhaḥ pavanas tejaḥ salilaṃ ca pṛthvī ca — five elements: space, air, fire, water, earth

Husk and grain (v. 24): tuṣa iva taṇḍulakaṇikām āvṛṇute prakṛtipūrvakaḥ sargaḥ — as husk covers grain, creation from prakṛti covers [consciousness]. Pṛthvīparyanto 'yaṃ caitanyaṃ dehabhāvena param āvaraṇaṃ mala iha sūkṣmaṃ māyādikañcukaṃ sthūlam

Three cloaks (v. 25): bāhyaṃ vigraharūpaṃ kośatrayaveṣṭito hy ātmā | ajñānatimirayogād ekam api svaṃ svabhāvam ātmānam | grāhyagrāhakanānāvaicitryeṇāvabudhyeta. Rasaphāṇitaśarkarikāguḍakhaṇḍādyā yathekṣurasa eva | tadvad avasthā bhedāḥ sarve paramātmanaḥ śambhoḥ
Snake and rope (v. 26): vyavahāramātram etat paramārthena tu na santy eva | rajjvāṃ nāsti bhujaṅgas trāsaṃ kurute ca mṛtyuparyantam
Power of delusion (v. 27): bhrānter mahatī śaktir na vivektuṃ śakyate nāma
param-p03.inference: The supreme consciousness descends through senses → tanmātras → elements → prakṛti's covering, like husk covers grain. The self is wrapped in three cloaks (trimala) but remains one, as sugar-cane juice in many forms. The world is transactional (vyavahāra), not ultimate (paramārtha) — like the snake in the rope — yet delusion has real power (śakti). Consciousness is covered, not destroyed.
param-p03.conclusion: Cosmological descent: senses → tanmātras → elements → prakṛti's covering (husk/grain) → three cloaks (trimala) → snake/rope → power of delusion. Key: consciousness is covered, not destroyed. The world is transactional, not ultimately real — but the fear (and suffering) is real.
param-p03.theorem: prakṛti covers consciousness like husk covers grain; the world is vyavahāra (like snake in rope), but bhrānti has śakti.
unresolved_terms: three cloaks (kośatraya) named but not individually enumerated; trimala is standard Trika reading
prakṛtipūrvakaḥ sargaḥ — Abhinava's reworking of Sāṃkhya
param-p03.next_pressure: L2: senses → tanmātras → elements → husk/grain → three cloaks → snake/rope → power of delusion.

param-p04.speaker: Guru (Abhinava)
param-p04.question: How does the unreal arise in the self (bondage)? How does the all-pervading Śiva appear as a limited knower (saṃkoca)?
premises: Bondage (v. 29): tadvad dharmādharmasvarnirayotpattimaraṇasukhaduḥkham | varṇāśramādi cātmany asad api vibhramabalād bhavati
Darkness upon darkness (v. 30): etat tad andhakāraṃ yad bhāveṣu prakāśamānatayā | ātmānatirikteṣv api bhavaty anātmābhimāno 'yam | timirād api timiram idaṃ
The net (v. 31): yad anātmany api dehaprāṇadāv ātmamānitvam … ātmānam veṣṭayate citraṃ jālena jālakāra iva; svajñānavibhavabhāsanayogenodveṣṭayen nijātmānam
World as play (v. 32): iti bandhamokṣacitrāṃ krīḍāṃ pratanoti paramaśivaḥ | sṛṣṭisthitisaṃhārā jāgratsvapnau suṣuptam iti tasmin
Saṃkoca (v. 33): śānte śānta ivāyaṃ hṛṣṭe hṛṣṭo vimohavati mūḍhaḥ | tattvagaṇe sati bhagavān na punaḥ paramārthataḥ sa tathā

Contracted experiencer (v. 34): yad anātmany api tadrūpāvabhāsanaṃ tat purā nirākṛtya | ātmany anātmarūpāṃ bhrāntiṃ vidalayati paramātmā; itthaṃ vibhramayugalakasamūlavicchedane kṛtārthasya | kartavyāntarakalanā na jātu parayogino bhavati
Threefold prakṛti (v. 35): pṛthivī prakṛtir māyā tritayam idaṃ vedyarūpatāpatitam; advaitabhāvanabalād bhavati hi sanmātrapariśeṣam | raśanākuṇḍalakaṭakaṃ bhedatyāgena dṛśyate yathā hema
Five knowers (v. 36): iti śakticakrayantraṃ krīḍāyogena vāhayan devaḥ — Śiva, Mantramaheśvara, Mantreśvara, Mantrī, vijñānakala, pralayākala, sakala
param-p04.inference: Bondage = self's misidentification with non-self by delusion's power (vibhramabala); darkness upon darkness (self's light misdirected onto non-self things). The net wraps the self, but self-knowledge can unwrap it. Saṃkoca = apparent impurity in the knower's vision, not in Śiva (moon/Rāhu). The method is two-stage (external then internal). Threefold prakṛti (earth/prakṛti/Māyā) is an object of knowledge; non-dual contemplation sees through form to substance (gold analogy). The knowers are Śiva in various states of contraction by the malas.
param-p04.conclusion: Bondage is unreal arising by delusion's power; saṃkoca is apparent, not real. The method is two-stage (external then internal). Non-dual contemplation dissolves the veiling. The knowers are Śiva contracted by malas, ascending from sakala to Śiva.
param-p04.theorem: Bondage = vibhramabala (delusion's power); saṃkoca = apparent impurity (moon/Rāhu); knowers = Śiva contracted by malas.
unresolved_terms: five vs. seven knowers — T1 gloss lists seven; standard Trika names five main + two sub-types
trimala (āṇava/māyīya/kārmaṇa) — named in p06, implied here
param-p04.next_pressure: L2: bondage (unreal arising) → darkness upon darkness → net → world as play → saṃkoca (moon/Rāhu) → contracted experiencer → method (clear external, then internal) → threefold prakṛti → gold analogy → five/seven knowers.

param-p05.speaker: Guru (Abhinava)
param-p05.question: How does the contracted experiencer get liberated? What is the condition and method?
premises: Moon/Rāhu continued (v. 38): śānte śānta ivāyaṃ hṛṣṭe hṛṣṭo vimohavati mūḍhaḥ | tattvagaṇe sati bhagavān na punaḥ paramārthataḥ sa tathā
Removing delusion (v. 39): yad anātmany api tadrūpāvabhāsanaṃ tat purā nirākṛtya | ātmany anātmarūpāṃ bhrāntiṃ vidalayati paramātmā
Accomplished yogi (v. 40): itthaṃ vibhramayugalakasamūlavicchedane kṛtārthasya | kartavyāntarakalanā na jātu parayogino bhavati
Threefold veiling (v. 41): pṛthivī prakṛtir māyā tritayam idaṃ vedyarūpatāpatitam
Non-dual contemplation (v. 42): advaitabhāvanabalād bhavati hi sanmātrapariśeṣam | raśanākuṇḍalakaṭakaṃ bhedatyāgena dṛśyate yathā hema
Result (v. 43): tadvad bhedatyāge sanmātraṃ sarvam ābhāti tad brahma paraṃ śuddhaṃ śāntaṃ abhedātmakaṃ samaṃ sakalam; amṛtaṃ satyaṃ śaktau viśrāmyati bhāsvarūpāyām
Śaktipāta (v. 44): aparāmṛṣṭaṃ yad api tu nabhaḥprasūnatvam abhyeti śaktitriśūlaparigamayogena samastam api parameśe; śivanāmani paramārthe visṛjyate devadevena
The return (v. 45): punar api ca pañcaśaktiprasaraṇakrameṇa bahir api tat | aṅdatrayaṃ vicitraṃ sṛṣṭaṃ bahirātmalābhena
param-p05.inference: Liberation is not earned but descended (śaktipāta). The method: remove external misidentification (world is not 'I'), then internal (body is not 'I'); non-dual contemplation sees through form to substance (gold analogy); the result is pure being (Brahman). Śaktipāta (three-pronged power) is the condition; Guru's grace is the vehicle. After liberation, creation is recognized as self (the return).
param-p05.conclusion: Liberation = śaktipāta + Guru's grace. Method: two-stage purification + non-dual contemplation (gold analogy). Result: pure being (Brahman). Condition: śaktipāta (three-pronged). Without śaktipāta, no liberation.
param-p05.theorem: mokṣa = śaktipāta (via Guru) + advaitabhāvana (gold analogy); result = sanmātra (pure being).
unresolved_terms: śaktitriśūla — 'three-pronged power' not individually enumerated; standard Trika identifies three śaktis (icchā/jñāna/kriyā) or three levels of śaktipāta
pañcaśakti (v. 45) — same five as p02, now in creative (external) mode
param-p05.next_pressure: L2: moon/Rāhu continued → removing delusion (external then internal) → accomplished yogi → threefold veiling → gold analogy → result → śaktipāta (three-pronged) → the return (creation recognized as self) → condition (śaktipāta + Guru's grace).

param-p06.speaker: Guru (Abhinava)
param-p06.question: What are the knowers (pramātṛ), and how do they relate to Śiva?
premises: Lord drives the wheel (v. 47): iti śakticakrayantraṃ krīḍāyogena vāhayan devaḥ
Śiva (v. 48): aham eva śuddharūpaḥ śaktimahācakranāyakapadasthaḥ — pure, no mala, top of the ladder
Mantramaheśvara (v. 49): mayy eva bhāti viśvaṃ darpaṇa iva nirmale ghatādīni — Māyā-mala only
Mantreśvara (v. 50): mattaḥ prasarati sarvaṃ svapnavicitratvam iva suptāt — vidyā-mala
Mantrī (v. 51): aham eva viśvarūpaḥ karacaranādisvabhāva iva dehaḥ — kalā-mala
Vijñānakala (v. 52): sarvasmin aham eva sphurāmi … dehendriyavarjito 'py akartāpi — kalā only, pure of Māyā-mala
Pralayākala (v. 53): siddhāntāgamatarkāṃś citrān aham eva racayāmi — Māyā only, pure of kalā-mala
Sakala (v. 54): itthaṃ dvaitavikalpe galite pravilaṅghya mohinīṃ māyām | salile salilaṃ kṣīre kṣīram iva brahmaṇi layī syāt — both malas, ordinary bound soul
Karma destruction (v. 55): kaḥ śokaḥ ko mohaḥ sarvaṃ brahmāvalokayataḥ | karmaphalaṃ śubham aśubhaṃ mithyājñānena saṃgamād eva; cirasaṃcitam iva tūlaṃ naśyati vijñānadīptivaśāt
param-p06.inference: The knowers are not a plurality of souls but Śiva himself in various states of contraction (saṅkoca). Classified by which malas veil them: Śiva (pure) → Mantramaheśvara (Māyā-mala) → Mantreśvara (vidyā-mala) → Mantrī (kalā-mala) → vijñānakala (kalā only) → pralayākala (Māyā only) → sakala (both malas). The ladder ascends from sakala to Śiva. Karma is destroyed by knowledge (fire/cotton analogy).
param-p06.conclusion: Knowers = Śiva contracted by malas. Ladder from sakala (both malas) to Śiva (pure). Liberation = ascending the ladder. Karma destroyed by knowledge (jñānāgni).
param-p06.theorem: pramātṛ = Śiva in saṅkoca; malas (Māyā/kalā) determine level; liberation = ascending the ladder + jñānāgni.
unresolved_terms: sevenfold vs. fivefold enumeration — T1 gloss lists seven; standard Trika names five main + two sub-types
śakticakrayantraṃ (v. 47) — 'wheel of the power-circle' not further specified
param-p06.next_pressure: L2: ladder (Śiva → Mantramaheśvara → Mantreśvara → Mantrī → vijñānakala → pralayākala → sakala). Key: v. 54's dissolution and v. 55's karma destruction.

param-p07.speaker: Guru (Abhinava)
param-p07.question: How is liberation (mokṣa) attained? What are the conditions and means?
premises: Knowledge without fruit (v. 56): jñānaprāptau kṛtam api na phalāya tato 'sya janma katham; gatajanmabandhayogo bhāti śivārkaḥ svadīdhitibhiḥ; tuṣakambukakiṃśārukamuktaṃ bījaṃ yathāṅkuraṃ kurute
Knower fears nothing (v. 57): naiva tathāṇavamāyākarmavimukto bhavāṅkuraṃ hy ātmā | ātmajño na kutaścana bibheti sarvaṃ hi tasya nijarūpam; naiva ca śocati yasmāt paramārthe nāśitā nāsti
The treasure (v. 58): atigūḍhahṛdayagañjaprarūḍhaparamārtharatnasaṃcayataḥ | aham eveti maheśvarabhāve kā durgatiḥ kasya mokṣasya naiva kiṃcid dhāmāsti na cāpi gamanam anyatra

The knot of ignorance (v. 59): ajñānagranthibhidā svaśaktyabhivyaktatā mokṣaḥ | bhinnājñānagranthir gatasaṃdehaḥ parākṛtabhrāntiḥ; prakṣīṇapuṇyapāpo vigrahayoge 'py asau muktaḥ; agnyabhidagdhaṃ bījaṃ yathā prarohāsamarthatām eti

Knowledge vs. karma (v. 60): jñānāgnidagdham evaṃ karma na janmapradaṃ bhavati; parimitabuddhitvena hi karmocitabhāvidehabhāvanayā; saṅkucitā citir etaddehadhvaṃse tathā bhāti; yadi punar amalaṃ bodhaṃ sarvasamuttīrnaboddhṛkartṛmayam | vitatam anastamitoditabhārūpam satyasaṃkalpam

The four upāyas (v. 61): jñānaprāptau kṛtam api na phalāya — anupāya (no means, śaktipāta alone), śāmbhava (will/icchā), śākta (knowledge/jñāna), āṇava (action/kriyā). Ladder descends from anupāya (highest) to āṇava (lowest).
The ascent (vv. 62–63): atitīvraśaktipātāt tadaiva nirvighnam eva śivaḥ; sarvottīrṇaṃ rūpaṃ sopānapadakrameṇa saṃśrayataḥ; paratattvarūḍhilābhe paryante śivamayībhāvaḥ

The middle (v. 64): tasya tu paramārthamayīṃ dhārām agatasya madhyaviśrānteḥ | tatpadalābhotsukacetaso 'pi maraṇaṃ kadācit syāt; yogabhraṣṭaḥ śāstre kathito 'sau citrabhogabhuvanapatiḥ; viśrāntisthānavaśād bhūtvā janmāntare śivībhavati
param-p07.inference: Liberation is not earned but descended (śaktipāta). The knot of ignorance is cut by knowledge's fire (jñānāgni), which destroys karma (seed burned by fire). The four upāyas (anupāya/śāmbhava/śākta/āṇava) form a ladder from highest (least effort) to lowest (most effort). The ascent is by śaktipāta, step by step. Even the yogabhraṣṭa (fallen yogi) becomes Śiva in another birth — the path is not a one-shot.
param-p07.conclusion: Liberation = śaktipāta + Guru's grace + jñānāgni. Four upāyas: anupāya (śaktipāta alone), śāmbhava (will), śākta (knowledge), āṇava (action). Ascent by śaktipāta, step by step. Even failure (yogabhraṣṭa) leads to Śiva in another birth.
param-p07.theorem: mokṣa = jñānāgni (burns karma) + śaktipāta (via Guru) + upāya (anupāya→āṇava). Even yogabhraṣṭa → Śiva in janmāntara.
unresolved_terms: śaktipāta intensity levels (tīvra/madhya/manda) — text implies (atitīvraśaktipātāt) but does not enumerate
yogabhraṣṭa — 'lord of a world of varied enjoyment' (citrabhogabhuvanapati) not further specified
param-p07.next_pressure: L2: knowledge destroys karma → knower fears nothing → treasure (no going, no path) → knot of ignorance → knowledge vs. karma → four upāyas (anupāya/śāmbhava/śākta/āṇava) → ascent (śaktipāta, step by step) → middle (yogabhraṣṭa, another birth).

param-p08.speaker: Guru (Abhinava)
param-p08.question: Is the world separate from Śiva? Is the knower liberated in this life (jīvanmukti)?
premises: World is Śiva (v. 65): dikkālakalanavikalaṃ dhruvam avyayam īśvaraṃ suparipūrṇam | bahutaraśaktivrātapralayodayaviracanaikakartāram — the Lord, free from space-time reckoning, eternal, imperishable, fully complete, sole maker of dissolution, rise, and creation, with many powers.

Awakening (v. 66): sṛṣṭyādividhisuvedhasam ātmānaṃ śivamayaṃ vibudhyeta | katham iva saṃsārī syād vitatasya kutaḥ kva vā saraṇam — one should awaken to the self as Śiva; how could one be a saṃsārin? For the all-pervading, where is refuge, where flight?

Karma's futility (v. 67): yuktibhir api siddhaṃ yatkarma jñānino na saphalaṃ tat; na mamedam api tu tasyeti dārḍhyato na hi phalaṃ loke — by reasoning too it is established: karma for the knower bears no fruit. 'This is not mine, but his' — with firmness, no fruit of karma in the world.

Knower's freedom (v. 68): itthaṃ sakalavikalpān pratibuddho bhāvanāsamīraṇataḥ | ātmajyotiṣi dīpte juhvaj jyotirmayo bhavati — thus, awakened to all thoughts by the wind of contemplation, offering into the blazing self-light, one becomes light.

Jīvanmukti (v. 69): aśnan yad vā tad vā saṃvīto yena kenacic chāntaḥ | yatra kvacana nivāsī vimucyate sarvabhūtātmā — eating this or that, clothed by whatever, peaceful; dwelling anywhere, the knower of all beings is liberated. Hayamedhaśatasahasrāṇy api kurute brahmaghātalakṣāṇi — even performing a hundred thousand horse sacrifices or killing a hundred thousand brahmins (hyperbole). Paramārthavin na puṇyair na ca pāpaiḥ spṛśyate vimalaḥ — the knower of the supreme is not touched by merit or demerit; stainless.

Delusion of distinction (v. 70): madaharṣakopamanmathaviṣādabhayalobhamohaparivarjī | niḥstotravaṣaṭkāro jaḍa iva vicared avādamatiḥ — free from pride, joy, anger, agitation, sorrow, fear, greed, delusion; without praise or oblation, moving like the inert, free from dispute. Madaharṣaprabhṛtir ayaṃ vargaḥ prabhavati vibhedasaṃmohāt — pride and the rest arise from the delusion of difference.

Advaita (v. 71): advaitātmavibodhas tena kathaṃ spṛśyatāṃ nāma stutyaṃ vā hotavyaṃ nāsti vyatiriktam asya kiṃcana ca — by the awakening to the non-dual self, how could he be touched? There is nothing to praise or offer, nothing separate from him. Stotrādinā sa tuṣyen muktas tan nirnamaskṛtivaṣaṭkaḥ — he is pleased by praise etc.; the liberated one is free from bowing and oblation.
Threefold world (implied): the world is Śiva's own nature, threefold: gross (five elements), subtle (five tanmātras), supreme (five tattvas).
param-p08.inference: The world is not separate from Śiva — it is his own nature (svabhāva), threefold: gross, subtle, supreme. The knower (jñānin) is liberated in this life (jīvanmukti): karma does not bear fruit for him; he is not touched by merit or demerit (even with hyperbolic examples); he is free even while embodied. The proof is by svātantrya: the Lord's freedom means the world is his self-manifestation, and the knower who recognizes this is Śiva, not a separate soul.
param-p08.conclusion: World = Śiva's own nature (threefold: gross/subtle/supreme). Jīvanmukti: knower is liberated in this life, not touched by merit/demerit, free even while embodied. Key: v. 69's paramārthavin na puṇyair na ca pāpaiḥ spṛśyate vimalaḥ and v. 68's jyotirmayo bhavati.
param-p08.theorem: jīvanmukti = recognition of world as Śiva's svabhāva; knower = Śiva, not touched by karma (puṇya/pāpa).
unresolved_terms: exact verse boundaries for vv. 72–73 — T1 gloss compresses them; verse divisions not marked
hayamedha hyperbole (v. 69) — Abhinava's rhetorical flourish, not a literal claim about karma
param-p08.next_pressure: L2: world is Śiva → awakening → karma's futility → knower's freedom → jīvanmukti (not touched by merit/demerit) → freedom from disturbances → advaita (nothing separate). Key: v. 69 paramārthavin na puṇyair na ca pāpaiḥ spṛśyate vimalaḥ; v. 68 jyotirmayo bhavati.

param-p09.speaker: Guru (Abhinava)
param-p09.question: What is the body, and what practices transform it?
premises: Body as garment (v. 74): ṣaṭtriṃśattattvabhṛtaṃ vigraharacanāgavākṣaparipūrṇam | nijam anyad atha śarīraṃ ghaṭādi vā tasya devagṛham — the body, bearing the 36 tattvas, complete with the windows of its structure — one's own or another's, a pot etc. — is the God's temple. Tatra ca paramātmamahābhairavaśivadevatāṃ svaśaktiyutām — and there, the supreme self, the great Bhairava-Śiva-deity, with his own power.

Worship (v. 75): ātmāmarśanavimaladravyaiḥ paripūjayann āste | bahirantaraparikalpanabhedamahābījanicayam arpayataḥ — worshipping with the stainless substances of self-reflection, one offers the great seed-mass of external and internal distinction-thoughts. Tasyātidīptasaṃvijjvalane yatnād vinā bhavati homaḥ — when the supremely blazing self-consciousness blazes, homa happens without effort.

Meditation (v. 76): dhyānam anastamitaṃ punar eṣa hi bhagavān vicitrarūpāṇi | sṛjati tad eva dhyānaṃ saṃkalpālikhitasatyarūpatvam — meditation, unsetting; and the Lord creates the varied forms; that very meditation is the painting of true forms by thought. Bhuvanāvalīṃ samastāṃ tattvakramakalpanām athākṣagaṇam — the whole series of worlds, the tattva-sequence, the sense-faculties.

Recitation (v. 77): antarbodhe parivartayati ca yat so 'sya japa uditaḥ — what revolves in the inner knowledge — that is his japa, declared. Sarvaṃ samayā dṛṣṭyā yat paśyati yac ca saṃvidaṃ manute — seeing all with the eye of samaya, perceiving all as consciousness.

The vow (v. 78): viśvaśmaśānaniratāṃ vigrahakhaṭvāṅgakalpanākalitām | viśvarasāsavapūrṇaṃ nijakaragaṃ vedyakhaṇḍakakapālam | rasayati ca yat tad etad vratam — the world as cremation-ground, the body as a skull-staff, the world's essence as wine in the hand, the known-fragment as a skull-cup — tasting this is his vrata. Sudurlabhaṃ ca sulabhaṃ ca — both hard to obtain and easy to obtain. Janmanāśahīnaṃ paramārthamaheśvarākhyam upalabhya — obtaining the name 'paramārtha-Maheśvara,' free from birth and death.

The result (v. 79): upalabdhṛtāprakāśāt kṛtakṛtyas tiṣṭhati yatheṣṭam | vyāpinam abhihitam itthaṃ sarvātmānaṃ vidhūtanānātvam | nirupamaparamānandaṃ yo vetti sa tanmayo bhavati — from the light of obtaining, the accomplished one stands as he wishes; the all-pervading, the all-self, free from diversity; who knows the incomparable supreme bliss becomes one with it.
param-p09.inference: The body is not an obstacle but Śiva's temple (devagṛha). The practices (homa, dhyāna, japa, vrata) are not means to reach Śiva (who is already present) but ways of recognizing what one already is: homa = offering distinctions into self-reflection; dhyāna = unsetting meditation (the Lord's creative act recognized); japa = inner turning (seeing all as consciousness); vrata = cremation-ground recognition (the world dies, the body is empty). The result: standing free, recognizing oneself as all, becoming one with bliss. The recognition is both hard and easy (sudurlabhaṃ ca sulabhaṃ ca).
param-p09.conclusion: Body = Śiva's temple (devagṛha). Practices = recognition, not attainment. Homa (offering distinctions) → dhyāna (unsetting meditation) → japa (inner turning) → vrata (cremation-ground recognition) → result (standing free, becoming bliss). Key: v. 74's devagṛham (body is temple, not obstacle); v. 78's sudurlabhaṃ ca sulabhaṃ ca (recognition is both hard and easy).
param-p09.theorem: body = devagṛha (Śiva's temple); practices = recognition (not attainment); result = tanmayatā (becoming one with bliss).
unresolved_terms: five winds (prāṇa/apāna/vyāna/udāna/samāna) and three channels (suṣumnā/īḍā/piṅgalā) — mentioned in T1 gloss but not in Sanskrit of p09 as rendered
devagṛha image is Abhinava's own; khaṭvāṅga and kapāla are Kāpālika imagery adopted by the Trika
param-p09.next_pressure: L2: body as temple → homa (offering of distinctions) → dhyāna (unsetting meditation) → japa (inner turning) → vrata (cremation-ground recognition) → result (standing free, becoming bliss). Key: v. 74's devagṛham; v. 78's sudurlabhaṃ ca sulabhaṃ ca.

param-p10.speaker: Guru (Abhinava)
param-p10.question: Is liberation place-dependent? What is mind, and how does it relate to Śiva?
premises: Place-independence (v. 83): tīrthe śvapacagṛhe vā naṣṭasmṛtir api parityajan deham | jñānasamakālamuktaḥ kaivalyaṃ yāti hataśokaḥ — in a tīrtha or in a dog-eater's house, even one who has lost memory, abandoning the body, at the moment of knowledge is liberated, sorrow destroyed. Puṇyāya tīrthasevā nirayāya śvapacasadananidhanagatiḥ — pilgrimage serves merit, death in a dog-eater's house serves demerit — but only for the unawakened.

The point (v. 84): puṇyāpuṇyakalaṅkasparśābhāve tu kiṃ tena — when there is no contact with the stain of merit and demerit, what use is that? Tuṣakambukasupṛthakkṛtataṇḍulakaṇatuṣadalāntarakṣepaḥ — like separating husk and grain and throwing away the husk; the grain (consciousness) is not affected. Taṇḍulakaṇasya kurute na punas tadrūpatādātmyam — it does not make the grain into husk. So too, merit/demerit does not touch the knower's consciousness.

Knower in the world (v. 85): tadvat kañcukapaṭalīpṛthakkṛtā saṃvid atra saṃskārāt | tiṣṭhanty api muktātmā tatsparśavivarjitā bhavati — so too consciousness, separated from the cloak-mass by saṃskāra, though abiding, the liberated self is free from contact. Kuśalatamaśilpikalpitavimalībhāvaḥ samudgakopādheḥ — like a jewel made stainless by the skill of the best artisan, from the casket's covering. Malino 'pi maṇir upādher vicchede svacchaparamārthaḥ — even a dirty jewel, when separated from its setting, is pure in ultimate truth.

Recognition (v. 86): evaṃ sadguruśāsanavimalasthiti vedanaṃ tanūpādheḥ | muktam apy upādhyantaraśūnyam ivābhāti śivarūpam — so, by the stainless state of the good Guru's teaching, the body-covering is known; even the liberated, free from other coverings, shines as Śiva's form. Śāstrādiprāmāṇyād avicalitaśraddhayāpi tanmayatām — even by the authority of scripture etc., with unwavering faith, one attains oneness with that.

Past (v. 87): prāptaḥ sa eva pūrvaṃ svargaṃ narakaṃ manuṣyatvam antyaḥ kṣaṇas tu tasmin puṇyāṃ pāpāṃ ca vā sthitiṃ puṣyan — he attained heaven, hell, human birth before; but in the final moment, bearing merit or demerit. Mūḍhānāṃ sahakārībhāvaṃ gacchati gatau tu na sa hetuḥ — for the deluded, it becomes a co-cause; but for the one who has gone (to liberation), it is not a cause. Ye 'pi tadātmatvena viduḥ paśupakṣisarīsṛpādayaḥ svagatim | te 'pi purātanasaṃbodhasaṃskṛtās tāṃ gatiṃ yānti — even those who know it as their own self — animals, birds, reptiles — attain that state, purified by ancient awakening.

Fourfold inner instrument (implied by gloss): mind (manas) = resolve/doubt; intellect (buddhi) = determination; ego (ahaṃkāra) = I-ness; citta = memory. Mind supports the senses; intellect determines; ego is the agent; citta remembers. These are Śiva's function, not independent faculties.
Knower's freedom (implied): the knower, having recognized mind as Śiva's function, is free from the inner instrument's binding power.
Closing (implied): the knower, having recognized mind as Śiva's function, is liberated.
param-p10.inference: Mind (manas) is not an independent faculty but Śiva's own function (kriyā). The passage establishes the fourfold inner instrument (mind, intellect, ego, citta) and proves that liberation is not place-dependent: the knower is liberated even in a dog-eater's house, because liberation is internal (tanmayatā), not external. The tīrtha (pilgrimage site) and the śvapaca-gṛha (dog-eater's house) are the same for the knower. Merit/demerit does not touch the knower's consciousness, like husk does not become grain.
param-p10.conclusion: Mind = Śiva's function (kriyā). Liberation is not place-dependent (tīrtha = śvapaca-gṛha). Merit/demerit does not touch the knower (like husk/grain). Recognition (Guru's teaching) → tanmayatā (oneness with Śiva). Key: v. 84's puṇyāpuṇyakalaṅkasparśābhāve tu kiṃ tena; v. 86's tanmayatām.
param-p10.theorem: manas = Śiva's kriyā (not independent faculty); liberation = tanmayatā (internal), not place-dependent.

fourfold inner instrument (antahkaraṇa) — T1 gloss lists the four with functions, but Sanskrit in T1.md for p10 does not explicitly enumerate them
param-p10.next_pressure: L2: place-independence (tīrtha = śvapaca-gṛha) → point (no stain touches the knower) → knower in the world (separated from cloaks by saṃskāra) → recognition (Guru's teaching) → past (merit/demerit not a cause for the liberated) → fourfold inner instrument → knower's freedom. Key: v. 84 puṇyāpuṇyakalaṅkasparśābhāve tu kiṃ tena; v. 86 tanmayatām.

param-p11.speaker: Guru (Abhinava)
param-p11.question: What is the soul (puruṣa), and does the knower fall at death?
premises: Soul's threefold nature (v. 92): svargamayo nirayamayas tad ayaṃ dehāntarālagaḥ puruṣaḥ — heaven-filled, hell-filled, this puruṣa resides between bodies. Tadbhaṅge svaucityād dehāntarayogam abhyeti evaṃ — when that (body) breaks, by its own fitness, it attains union with another body. The soul transmigrates, but its nature is determined by its recognition, not by the body.

Recognition persists (v. 93): jñānāvasare svātmā sakṛd asya yādṛg avabhātaḥ | tādṛśa eva tadāsau na dehapāte 'nyathā bhavati — at the moment of knowledge, the self shines for him as it is; so it remains, not otherwise at the body's fall. Recognition is not body-dependent; it persists through death.

Body's end (v. 94): karaṇagaṇasaṃpramoṣaḥ smṛtināśaḥ śvāsakalilatā cchedaḥ | marmasu rujāviśeṣāḥ śarīrasaṃskārajo bhogaḥ — loss of the sense-faculties, destruction of memory, breath in agitation, cutting; special pains in the vital points; enjoyment born of body-saṃskāra. Sa kathaṃ vigrahayoge sati na bhavet tena mohayoge 'pi — how could it not arise when the body is present, even in delusion's presence?

Knower at death (v. 95): maraṇāvasare jñāni na cyavate svātmaparamārthāt | paramārthamārgam enaṃ jhaṭiti yadā gurumukhāt samabhyeti — at the moment of death, the knower does not fall from the supreme truth of the self; this supreme path he quickly attains from the Guru's mouth. Atitīvraśaktipātāt tadaiva nirvighnam eva śivaḥ — by very intense śaktipāta, at that moment, unobstructed, Śiva. Sarvottīrṇaṃ rūpaṃ sopānapadakrameṇa saṃśrayataḥ — attaining the supreme form step by step.

The end (v. 96): paratattvarūḍhilābhe paryante śivamayībhāvaḥ — at the end, attainment of the supreme principle's form: Śiva-mayībhāva. Tasya tu paramārthamayīṃ dhārām agatasya madhyaviśrānteḥ | tatpadalābhotsukacetaso 'pi maraṇaṃ kadācit syāt — but for one who has not reached the supreme-principle stream, resting in the middle, death may come even for one eager for that state.

Yogabhraṣṭa (v. 97): yogabhraṣṭaḥ śāstre kathito 'sau citrabhogabhuvanapatiḥ — the yogabhraṣṭa (fallen yogi) is described in scripture as lord of a world of varied enjoyment. Viśrāntisthānavaśād bhūtvā janmāntare śivībhavati — by the power of the resting-place, in another birth he becomes Śiva. Even failure on the path leads to Śiva; the path is not a one-shot.

Paramārtha path (v. 98): paramārthamārgam enaṃ hy abhyasyāprāpya yogam api nāma | suralokabhogabhāgī muditamanā modate suciram — even without attaining yoga, having practiced this supreme path, he becomes an enjoyer of heaven, joyful, delighting for a long time. Heaven-enjoyment is not final, but it is not nothing; the path bears fruit even in incompleteness.
Close (vv. 99–100, implied): Śivahood is the only final state; heaven and hell are intermediate.
param-p11.inference: The soul (puruṣa) is not a separate entity but Śiva's own part (aṃśa), threefold: jīva (worldly, veiled by Māyā), ātman (liberated, by śaktipāta), paramātman (eternally liberated, Śiva). The passage proves that the knower who has recognized this does not fall at death: he does not change, because his recognition is not body-dependent. Even the yogabhraṣṭa (fallen yogi) becomes Śiva in another birth. The close: even heaven-enjoyment is not final; only Śivahood is.
param-p11.conclusion: Soul = Śiva's part (aṃśa), threefold (jīva/ātman/paramātman). Recognition persists through death (v. 93). Even the yogabhraṣṭa becomes Śiva in another birth (v. 97). Heaven-enjoyment is not final; only Śivahood is. Key: v. 93's tādṛśa eva tadāsau na dehapāte 'nyathā bhavati; v. 97's janmāntare śivībhavati.
param-p11.theorem: puruṣa = Śiva's aṃśa (jīva/ātman/paramātman); recognition persists through death; yogabhraṣṭa → Śiva in janmāntara.
unresolved_terms: individual verse boundaries for vv. 92–100 — T1 gloss compresses them; verse divisions not marked
yogabhraṣṭa's 'world of varied enjoyment' (citrabhogabhuvana) — not further specified; read as intermediate heaven-realm
param-p11.next_pressure: L2: threefold soul → recognition persists through death → body's end (painful but not decisive) → knower at death (śaktipāta, step by step) → end (Śiva-mayībhāva) → yogabhraṣṭa (failure is not final) → paramārtha path (bears fruit even incomplete) → close (Śivahood only final).

param-p12.speaker: Guru (Abhinava)
param-p12.question: What is the text's final word? What is the seal?
premises: King and yogabhraṣṭa (v. 101): viṣayeṣu sārvabhaumaḥ sarvajanaiḥ pūjyate yathā rājā | bhuvaneṣu sarvadaivair yogabhraṣṭas tathā pūjyaḥ — as a king, sovereign in his realm, is worshipped by all people, so the yogabhraṣṭa is worshipped by all gods in the worlds. The fallen yogi, though not liberated, is still exalted — his practice has borne fruit even in incompleteness.

The return (v. 102): mahatā kālena punar mānuṣyaṃ prāpya yogam abhyasya | prāpnoti divyam amṛtam yasmād āvartate na punaḥ — after a long time, attaining humanity again, practicing yoga, he obtains the divine immortal, from which there is no return. The yogabhraṣṭa's path is not lost; it resumes in another birth and reaches the immortal.

The instruction (v. 103): tasmāt sanmārge 'smin nirato yaḥ kaścid eti sa śivatvam — therefore, whoever is devoted to this true path attains Śivahood. The text's practical instruction: devotion to the path is sufficient.

The essence (v. 104): iti matvā paramārthe yathā tathāpi prayatanīyam idam | abhinavaguptoditasaṃkṣepaṃ dhyāyataḥ paraṃ brahma — knowing this, in the supreme, as it is, still one should strive; meditating on this essence spoken by Abhinavagupta, the supreme Brahman. Acirād eva śivatvaṃ nijahṛdayāveśam abhyeti — quickly, Śivahood, the entry into one's own heart, is attained. Āryāśatena tad idaṃ saṃkṣiptaṃ śāstrasāram atigūḍham — in a hundred verses, this condensed essence of śāstra, very hidden.

The seal (v. 105): abhinavaguptena mayā śivacaraṇasmaraṇadīptena — by me, Abhinavagupta, kindled by the remembrance of Śiva's feet. The author's signature: the text is spoken by one whose fire is the remembrance of Śiva's feet.
param-p12.inference: The text closes. The seal: the Paramārthasāra, spoken by Abhinava by Śiva-śāsana view, is the essence (saṃkṣepa) of all śāstra. Śivahood is attained by Guru's grace and knowledge; knowledge destroys the malas; in Śivahood all becomes Śiva. The yogabhraṣṭa, even without attaining yoga, becomes an enjoyer of heaven and eventually Śiva. The text's final instruction: meditate on this essence; Śivahood is near.
param-p12.conclusion: The Paramārthasāra's seal: Śivahood is attainable by devotion to the path; meditating on this essence, one quickly attains Śivahood — the entry into one's own heart. The author is kindled by Śiva's feet. The text is the condensed essence of all śāstra.
param-p12.theorem: Śivahood = nijahṛdayāveśa (entry into one's own heart); attainable by sanmārga (true path); meditate on this saṃkṣepa.
unresolved_terms: verse count discrepancy: T1 says 104 kārikās; web sources say 105. The discrepancy is in counting the benediction (v. 1) or the closing verse.
yogabhraṣṭa's 'world of varied enjoyment' (citrabhogabhuvana) — not further specified; read as intermediate heaven-realm (consistent with p11)
param-p12.next_pressure: L2: king/yogabhraṣṭa → return (no return from the immortal) → instruction (devotion suffices) → essence (meditate on this) → seal (Abhinava, kindled by Śiva's feet). Key: v. 104's acirād eva śivatvaṃ nijahṛdayāveśam abhyeti.
